clue.text: See addict transformed, without minimal cocaine, totally dried out

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters sit around the cocaine piece
transformed says the letters of see addict are made over into a new order
minimal cocaine is the least of the word, just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A warning to an addict that cutting back on cocaine has left them completely dried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges SEE ADDICT, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps those letters round C, the first letter of cocaine picked out by 'minimal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiccated means having had all moisture removed, so totally dried out is a direct synonym.

clue.text: End of ten years going round India, abandoning Dhaka finally

indicators.note: abandoning says a letter is dropped from the word built so far
going round says the ten-year word encircles the India letter

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of Dhaka

explanation.surface: A decade of travel around India comes to an end as the traveller leaves Dhaka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts I inside DECADE, and 'abandoning' then drops A, the last letter of Dhaka picked by 'finally'. 'End' is a verb here: to settle a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide a contest or dispute is to bring it to a conclusion, so decide can mean end.

clue.text: Line in article probing religious group

indicators.note: probing pictures one piece pushing its way into another

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece digging into the affairs of a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a line of print in the article, but it is the geometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a secant is a straight line that cuts a curve at two or more points.

clue.text: Officials organising lesbian march

indicators.note: organising suggests putting the letters of lesbian march into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Officials who are arranging a lesbian march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges LESBIAN MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlains are officers who manage a royal or noble household, so they are officials.

clue.text: Hairstyle upset some poor father

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poor father is upset about a particular hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ORFA from 'poor father' and 'upset', in a down clue, turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle of tightly curled hair.

clue.text: Eastern guru includes talk about drug confiscation of yesteryear

indicators.note: includes says the guru word holds the talk-and-drug group within it

parts.note: a guru is a sage, a wise teacher

indicators.note: about says the talk word goes round the drug letter

parts.note: to chat is to talk
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An Eastern guru admits chatting about drugs, and something is confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the talk word round ecstasy to make CHEAT, which 'includes' sets in the guru word. E for ecstasy is common slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheatage was the old right of a lord to take over land when a tenant died without heirs, an archaic forfeiture.

clue.text: Spring maiden to send out unwanted message?

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman in spring sending an unwanted note to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spam is to send junk email or other unsolicited messages in bulk.

clue.text: Superior group capsized, stuck in vessel — it could suggest an emergency

indicators.note: stuck in says the turned letters are lodged inside the vessel word

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

indicators.note: capsized, in a down clue, says the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior
a crew is a group, such as a ship's team

explanation.surface: A boat's elite crew capsize and are stuck in their vessel, a clear emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns the superior group upside down to give WERCU, which is 'stuck in' the vessel. U for upper class is an old British label for posh speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut, a loss of mains electricity, is the sort of event that can count as an emergency.

clue.text: Our state perhaps gets wealth, English being cunning

indicators.note: being here says the English letter becomes the cunning word, one standing in for the other

parts.note: money is wealth
arch means sly or knowingly cunning

explanation.surface: A British observation that our nation thrives on wealth and English cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' replaces the E of MONEY with ARCH. The setter writes for a British paper, so 'our state' is the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is a monarchy, a state headed by a king or queen, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Monster bird — a number of times it crowed — hard to forget

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: to forget says a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: thrice, three times, recalls the cockcrow tied to Peter's three denials in the Gospels
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A monstrous bird is described crowing a number of times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forget' drops H from THRICE. 'Monster bird' looks like one phrase, but the bird is the cock in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatrice is a mythical monster, a serpent hatched from a cock's egg whose glance could kill.

clue.text: Swimmer in river down below

definitions.meaning: the river flowing through Perth, Australia, the land 'down under'

explanation.walkthrough: 'down below' is a play on Down Under, a nickname for Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan is a waterbird seen swimming, and the Swan River runs through Perth in Western Australia.

clue.text: Hero fought at clashes, as planned in advance

indicators.note: clashes suggests the letters of hero fought at colliding and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A hero fought in battles that had been planned ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clashes' rearranges HERO FOUGHT AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforethought, as in malice aforethought, means premeditated, thought out beforehand.

clue.text: Flower to fade, one fading with a small lump inside

indicators.note: inside says these letters go within what is left
fading says the one letter disappears from the word

parts.note: to die away is to fade
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nub is a small lump

explanation.surface: A flower wilting, with one bloom drooping and a small lump inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fading' drops the I to leave DE, and 'inside' fills it. 'Flower' is a crossword pun: something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is one of Europe's great rivers, and a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Sailor with someone wise circling in the distance

indicators.note: circling says the wise person's word surrounds the distance word

parts.note: a seer is a wise person who can see the future
afar means far away, in the distance

explanation.surface: A sailor joined by a wise companion, sailing round somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' has the wise one surround the distance word; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a person who travels by sea, especially as a regular sailor.

clue.text: Like cross-country train during good regular trip

parts.note: over means during, as in over the weekend
a round is a regular trip, like a milk or postal round

explanation.surface: Taking a cross-country train during a good, regular journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is a regular route of calls, as a British milkman's or postman's daily round.
explanation.definitionFit: An overground train runs on the surface rather than underground, as a cross-country service does.

clue.text: Forcefully introduce facility for hungry travellers?

definitions.meaning: to ... a measure is to push it in by force
a ... is a restaurant serving customers in their cars

explanation.definitionFit: To drive something through is to force it in or push it past opposition; a drive-through is a fast-food counter for motorists.

clue.text: Character, one with worry getting upset — buttoned-up type?

parts.note: a card is a character, an amusing eccentric
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: getting upset, in a down clue, says the worry word is turned upside down

parts.note: to nag is to worry, to pester

explanation.surface: A buttoned-up character who frets about everything gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns NAG into GAN. 'Buttoned-up' suggests a repressed person, but it is a garment with buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket fastened with buttons down the front, a buttoned-up type of garment.

clue.text: Crooner with suppressed longing is complaining

indicators.note: with suppressed says the crooner holds the longing word hidden within

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous crooner
an itch is a longing, a restless desire

explanation.surface: A singer keeps his desires in check, and so is always moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The crooner is Bing Crosby; 'with suppressed' holds the longing inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitching is slang for complaining spitefully or constantly.

clue.text: Ram is halting, in trouble — what is called upon to stop the beast suffering?

definitions.text: what is called upon to stop the beast suffering?

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of ram is halting being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ram is limping and in distress, and someone appeals to stop the creature suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges RAM IS HALTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal rights campaigners invoke the principle that creatures deserve protection from cruelty.

clue.text: Journey ends in hotel — 'The Peal of Bells'

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: ends in picks the final letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A journey ends at a hotel called The Peal of Bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends in' takes L and E, the last letters of 'hotel' and 'The'. The quotation marks make it look like a pub or hotel name.
explanation.definitionFit: Triples is a change-ringing method on seven bells, so a triple names a kind of peal.

clue.text: Wild cricket shots or nicks?

definitions.meaning: a swipe is a wild swinging stroke of the bat
to nick is to steal, and ... means steals too

explanation.walkthrough: Nicks is British slang for steals; in cricket a nick is also a faint edge off the bat, the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: A swipe is a reckless slog in cricket, and to swipe something is to pilfer it.

clue.text: Plant providing nectar, I'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters of nectar I'd are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imagining a plant that yields nectar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges NECTAR I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicentra is a genus of flowering plants that includes bleeding heart and Dutchman's breeches.

clue.text: Kind to waste time and quarrel that could make you weep

indicators.note: to waste time here says the time letter is thrown away

parts.note: sort means kind, type
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Wasting time and arguing is the kind of thing that leaves you in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to waste' drops T from SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is deep grief or sadness, the kind of feeling that brings tears.

clue.text: Painter of optical illusions offering nothing for a long time

indicators.note: for says the nothing letter replaces the long-time word

parts.note: mirages are optical illusions
ages means a long time
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A painter of optical illusions has produced nothing for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the zero in for the long time. 'Painter of optical illusions' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Painter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a Spanish artist known for colourful surrealist paintings.

clue.text: Hold on to final message by the side of grave

indicators.note: side of picks the edge letter of grave, its first

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the final message on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Clinging to a last message at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side of' gives G, the first letter of 'grave'. 'on to' and 'by' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a firm hold, as in losing your grip on something.

clue.text: Being swindled, as pet-shop customer might be?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being cheated in a deal
taken literally, a customer at a pet shop could be buying a young dog

explanation.definitionFit: To buy a pup is a British and Australian idiom for being conned; read literally it is purchasing a puppy.

clue.text: Eggy drink with extra egg not allowed

parts.note: nog, as in eggnog, is a drink made with eggs
O resembles an egg by its shape

explanation.surface: An egg drink with another egg added is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for an egg because of its oval shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area or plan is one that is forbidden or ruled out.

clue.text: Skill of a GP? Nothing to it, Bill!

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, DR
O, zero, is nothing
a ness is a headland, and so is a bill, as in Portland Bill

explanation.surface: A doctor told there is nothing to his skill, addressing someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a promontory: Portland Bill is a headland on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness means dexterity or cleverness, a synonym of skill.
